checkpoint.measure: Score share against fixed practice opponents (0.5 = even)
checkpoint.tier_note: L3 here comes from the main run: its practice-player rows play at level L3 (no separate L3 runs).

skills.name: Aims at the call (seeing the balls + stroke direction)
skills.real: A player finds the balls by eye; the rules allow no measuring aid. One head colour camera, at most 12 views a shot; a few millimetres misread turn into tenths of a degree of aim.
skills.measure: Scenario pot: each stroke's direction at contact (, measured by the world) less the centre of the aims that pot the called ball in the called pocket, computed by the world (, the function L3 reads a player's error with); strokes with |error| ≤ 0.5 deg / strokes with a reading. Match Checkpoint Evaluations: aim_ok / aim_n (the same reading).
skills.line: ≥ 60 % of strokes within 0.5 deg (seeds pooled, ≥ 5 strokes with a reading)

skills.name: Pots the called ball (straight-in)
skills.real: Potting is the basic act of pool: see the balls, line up, stroke with the right speed and tip, and the ball drops in the called pocket.
skills.measure: Scenario pot, straight-in tables (even shots): the called ball is the laid one and it dropped in the called pocket / straight-in shots. Match Checkpoint Evaluations: pots_legal / shots.
skills.line: Straight-in ≥ 50 % made (seeds pooled, 6 shots); match Checkpoint Evaluations keep ≥ 30 %

skills.name: Pots a cut (30 deg)
skills.real: A cut needs the ghost-ball point and throw (friction between the balls drags the object ball off line); errors in seeing the balls grow with the cut.
skills.measure: Scenario pot, cut tables (odd shots, the cue ball on a 30 deg cut, alternating sides): made / cut shots.

skills.name: Clean strokes (two-handed bridge, no fall, in time)
skills.real: The rules want a legal stroke: the cue on a bridge, the tip meets the cue ball, the player stays up; each shot has a time limit.
skills.measure: All drill shots: the tip met the cue ball and the foul text names no stroke fault (fell, no bridge, shot clock, no contact) / shots. Match Checkpoint Evaluations: clean_strokes / shots. Falls (the old 'no fall while stroking') are part of this.

skills.name: Break power
skills.real: The break drives power into the rack: WPA 4.3 needs a ball potted or at least 4 object balls to a cushion, else it is a foul. The program breaks in half the matches.
skills.measure: Scenario break: the official rack ( of the drill seed), the program breaks from the kitchen; the mean number of object balls sent to a cushion per break ( = object_balls_to_cushion), with legal breaks and cue speed V0 aside. A break past the 120 s shot clock is not played and reads 0.
skills.line: Mean ≥ 3 balls to a cushion (seeds pooled, 4 breaks)

skills.name: Places the cue ball with ball in hand
skills.real: After the opponent's foul the cue ball goes anywhere: a good player gives itself a short, straight pot.
skills.measure: Scenario hand: the cue ball off the table, ball in hand anywhere, one own ball on the table; made / shots, with the shots where the program placed the cue ball itself and the median cut angle of its chosen pot (cue_placed_at, cut_deg).

skills.name: Legal shots
skills.real: WPA chapter 4: every shot called, own ball hit first, a cushion or a pot after it, the cue ball stays on the table.
skills.measure: All drill shots: no foul ( empty) / shots. Match Checkpoint Evaluations: legal / shots.

skills.name: Runs of pots (position play)
skills.real: Position play is the core of pool: pot one, leave the cue ball where the next is easy.
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluations only: runs2 (at least one visit with 2 pots, 2/3 of racks). No drill (single-shot drills do not test position).

skills.name: Effective safeties
skills.real: With no good pot, call safety and leave the opponent a hard table.
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluations only: safety_ok / safeties (a legal safety after which the opponent fouls or pots nothing).

skills.name: Shoots every turn in time
skills.real: The program must stroke within 120 s a shot and the match chess clock; no stroke loses. In Checkpoint Evaluations some programs crashed in their vision code and never acted again.
skills.measure: All drills: the drill finished (the scenario record, shots = cap), no shot past the shot clock ( / a 'shot clock' foul).

off.name: Walking to a new stance
off.why: Not tested: the robot is teleported to its chosen stance each shot (excluded on the card).

off.name: Real-time reaction
off.why: Not tested: pool is static between shots.

open_questions: Seat resources: the drill seat had 2 cores (re-tests 8, official 16), and the 5-core controls show the late shots come mainly from that. The proposal: rerun the break drill and Opus's three drills on an 8-core seat before settling these skills. Do it?
Break line: even the reference makes only 1 legal break of 4 under WPA; the proposal reads power as 'mean >= 3 balls to a cushion' and shows the legal rate aside. Or keep the rule's 4-ball line?
The 50 % lines for straight-in, cut and ball in hand are proposals; the reference reads 5/6, 6/6, 6/8, and every ablation arm falls below.

notes.challenge: Eight-ball on a full-size table for a humanoid without fingers. The program sees the balls with a head camera, plans the shot and strikes with a two-handed whole-body stroke.

achieved.text: Each model failed at a different stage; on non-break shots the cue reached the ball for Claude Opus 5.5 198 of 219 times, GPT-6 Astra 149 of 183, Kimi 3.1 Pro 162 of 249, Gemini 4 Argon 94 of 157, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 20 of 282 and GLM 5.3 Flash 13 of 166.
DeepSeek and GLM potted no ball all event, yet DeepSeek won three 7:7 clock tie-breaks; in BIL2-F15 its clock lead came mostly from answering reviews faster (69 %).
DeepSeek resigned four matches, the only resignations of the event; in one it reasoned that "the match is lost either way".
Opus's Championship stroke was the steadiest: 95 of 104 shots legal, with no fallback and no missed contact.

GLM 5.3 Flash: Moved its match reviews into its own program; the referee accepts reviews only from the agent and refused 9,232 of them in one match, while GLM kept sending reviews by hand.
Kimi 3.1 Pro: Wrote up to 1,710 files and 49 snapshots in one match; its Championship series fell apart: legal rest-bridge shots 16 of 24 in its fresh Arena matches against 28 of 82, called pots 5 to 0.

interface.sees: One head camera (1280 × 720), with up to 12 looks a shot from anywhere around the table, plus the referee's table facts and every shot's result. No ball coordinates.
interface.controls: One whole stroke per turn, sent before it starts: where the robot stands, the bridge, and targets for all 29 joints every 10 ms for up to 15 s. Turn-based: the table waits while the agent thinks.
interface.moment: Final, shot 13. Opus (solids, 5 left) looks along the table from the side rail before it calls the 7 into a corner pocket and pots it. A look moves only the camera, so the broadcast shows the robot already in its stance for the stroke.

camera.label: Robot camera · Opus · 1280 × 720 · a look before the shot

details: Camera: the real G1's head camera (an Intel RealSense D435i colour camera, 1280 × 720, 69.4° × 42.5°), fixed on the trunk and tilted 47.6° down. The G1 has no neck.

Looks: an observation shows the table from where the robot stands; a look places the robot anywhere legal around the table (position, facing, optional pose and bridge) to see it from there, up to 12 times a shot. Each image comes with the camera's exact pose and lens numbers.
Not given: where the balls are. The program finds every ball in the images.

Referee: shot number, balls on the table, who broke, each side's group and balls left, shots taken and the 60-shot limit, ball in hand, whether a side is on the 8, whether a call is required, and each shot since your last (first ball hit, balls potted and pockets, fouls, the call).

The stroke: where the robot stands (position on the floor and facing), the bridge (left hand on the cloth, hand on the rail, or a mechanical rest), and targets for all 29 joints, one row per 10 ms, up to 1500 rows (15 s).

Also in the stroke if wanted: joint speeds, extra torque, stiffness and damping, where the hand grips the cue, a cue extension of 0.30 or 0.60 m, and planned changes at chosen steps. Everything is decided before the stroke starts.
With ball in hand the stroke also places the cue ball; a called shot names the ball and the pocket, or a safety.

Nothing reaches the program during the stroke: the planned rows play out. Touching a ball with the robot, cue or bridge, no cue-ball contact within 15 s, a fall, or a cue that leaves the bridge is a foul.
Timing: turn-based. Nothing moves while the agent thinks; a 2-hour chess clock runs only on its turn, and a shot more than 120 s after its previous one is a foul.
Rules: WPA 8-ball, one rack, at most 60 shots each; after that, fewer balls left wins.
Before the match: 2 hours of preparation with a full practice copy of the table world and a practice opponent; the training kit runs on the CPU.
